Timeline::set_year¶

Back to Timeline API Reference

Signature¶

Timeline Timeline::set_year(int year) const

Replace The Civil Year¶

set_year() creates a new Timeline by replacing the year shown in every defined element’s local calendar. It is a field replacement, not elapsed-time arithmetic: month, day, clock fields, fractional nanoseconds, shape, element order, and timezone remain unchanged.

That distinction decides when to use it. Use set_year(2030) when every value must belong to calendar year 2030 while retaining its other fields. Use a calendar offset when the instruction is instead “move each value forward by some number of years.”

Replacement is strict. A result must be a real local date for every defined element. Replacing the year of 2024-02-29 with 2023 therefore throws; the method does not silently choose 28 February. Absent instants remain absent and do not participate in calendar validation.

Example: Replace One Field, Preserve The Rest¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::make("2024-06-20T04:05:06.000000004Z");
const auto changed = t.set_year(2030);

auto options = pluss::timeline::FormatOptions{};
options.pattern = "%FT%T.%f%z";
std::cout << pluss::timeline::format(changed, options).at(0) << '\n';

Output¶

2030-06-20T04:05:06.000000004+00:00

The four trailing nanoseconds are intentionally visible: replacing a calendar field does not reduce timestamp precision.

Example: The Scalar Applies To Every Element¶

const auto t = pluss::timeline::make({
    {"2024-01-15T23:58:59.123456789Z", "2024-06-20T04:05:06.000000004Z"},
    {"2024-09-28T12:30:45.900000000Z", "2024-12-01T00:00:00.000000001Z"},
});
const auto changed = t.set_year(2030);

std::cout << pluss::note::print(
    pluss::timeline::format(changed, "%FT%T.%f%z")) << '\n';

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 2], dim=2, numel=4, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["2030-01-15T23:58:59.123456789+00:00", "2030-06-20T04:05:06.000000004+00:00"], 
  ["2030-09-28T12:30:45.900000000+00:00", "2030-12-01T00:00:00.000000001+00:00"]
]

year is one scalar argument, not a per-element Series. The same year is used at every logical position, including positions reached through a strided view. The receiver is unchanged and the result owns its replacement values.

Example: Invalid Leap-Day Replacement¶

try {
  const auto leap = pluss::timeline::make("2024-02-29T12:00:00Z");
  (void)leap.set_year(2023);
} catch (const pluss::Error&) {
  std::cout << "invalid calendar date rejected\n";
}

Output¶

invalid calendar date rejected

The operation is all-or-nothing from the caller’s perspective: no partly modified Timeline is returned if any defined element would become invalid. The year argument itself is validated even when the receiver is empty.

Timezones And Local Calendars¶

The replaced field is the year in tz(), not a year extracted from raw UTC ticks. The timezone label is retained. Reconstructing the local date may select a different UTC offset if that date belongs to a different daylight-saving period. This is calendar editing, so preserving wall-clock fields takes priority over preserving the original elapsed offset from UTC.

See Also¶

  • year: inspect the local civil year.

  • set_month: replace the month without changing the year.

  • tz_convert: change the calendar view without changing instants.
